"""Language-specific transliteration tables used when building slugs.

Unicode normalisation (NFKD followed by dropping combining marks) handles
most accented Latin letters correctly, but some letters are conventionally
written differently depending on the language. German "ü" is usually "ue",
whereas in French or Turkish it is simply "u". Letters such as "ø", "ß" or
"đ" have no decomposition at all and would otherwise be lost.

This module keeps one mapping per language code. A table is applied before
generic normalisation so that language rules take priority.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import unicodedata
from typing import Dict, Mapping, Optional

# Characters that most languages treat identically. These have no Unicode
# decomposition, so they must be listed explicitly.
_COMMON: Dict[str, str] = {
    "æ": "ae", "Æ": "AE",
    "œ": "oe", "Œ": "OE",
    "ð": "d", "Ð": "D",
    "þ": "th", "Þ": "TH",
    "ł": "l", "Ł": "L",
    "đ": "d", "Đ": "D",
    "ß": "ss",
}

_GERMAN: Dict[str, str] = {
    "ä": "ae", "Ä": "Ae",
    "ö": "oe", "Ö": "Oe",
    "ü": "ue", "Ü": "Ue",
}

_SCANDINAVIAN: Dict[str, str] = {
    "å": "aa", "Å": "Aa",
    "ø": "oe", "Ø": "Oe",
    "æ": "ae", "Æ": "Ae",
}

_SWEDISH: Dict[str, str] = {
    "å": "a", "Å": "A",
    "ä": "a", "Ä": "A",
    "ö": "o", "Ö": "O",
}

_TURKISH: Dict[str, str] = {
    "ı": "i", "İ": "I",
    "ş": "s", "Ş": "S",
    "ğ": "g", "Ğ": "G",
    "ç": "c", "Ç": "C",
}

_RUSSIAN: Dict[str, str] = {
    "а": "a", "б": "b", "в": "v", "г": "g", "д": "d", "е": "e",
    "ё": "yo", "ж": "zh", "з": "z", "и": "i", "й": "y", "к": "k",
    "л": "l", "м": "m", "н": "n", "о": "o", "п": "p", "р": "r",
    "с": "s", "т": "t", "у": "u", "ф": "f", "х": "kh", "ц": "ts",
    "ч": "ch", "ш": "sh", "щ": "shch", "ъ": "", "ы": "y", "ь": "",
    "э": "e", "ю": "yu", "я": "ya",
}

# Upper-case Cyrillic is derived from the lower-case entries below.
for _lower, _latin in list(_RUSSIAN.items()):
    _RUSSIAN[_lower.upper()] = _latin.capitalize()

_TABLES: Dict[str, Mapping[str, str]] = {
    "de": _GERMAN,
    "da": _SCANDINAVIAN,
    "nb": _SCANDINAVIAN,
    "no": _SCANDINAVIAN,
    "sv": _SWEDISH,
    "tr": _TURKISH,
    "ru": _RUSSIAN,
}

# Compiled translation tables, built lazily and cached per language code.
_COMPILED: Dict[Optional[str], Dict[int, str]] = {}


def register_table(lang: str, table: Mapping[str, str]) -> None:
    """Register or replace the transliteration table for ``lang``.

    Keys must be single characters. Values may be empty strings, in which
    case the character is removed from the output.
    """
    for key in table:
        if len(key) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"table keys must be single characters: {key!r}")
    _TABLES[lang.lower()] = dict(table)
    _COMPILED.clear()


def _normalise_lang(lang: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    """Reduce a locale such as ``de_DE`` or ``pt-BR`` to its language code."""
    if not lang:
        return None
    for separator in ("_", "-"):
        lang = lang.split(separator)[0]
    return lang.lower()


def get_table(lang: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[int, str]:
    """Return a ``str.translate`` table for ``lang``.

    Language-specific entries override the common entries. An unknown or
    missing language yields the common table only.
    """
    code = _normalise_lang(lang)
    if code not in _COMPILED:
        merged: Dict[str, str] = dict(_COMMON)
        merged.update(_TABLES.get(code, {}))
        _COMPILED[code] = {ord(k): v for k, v in merged.items()}
    return _COMPILED[code]


def transliterate(text: str, lang: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """Convert ``text`` to ASCII using the rules for ``lang``.

    Language rules are applied first. Remaining accented characters are
    decomposed and their combining marks removed. Characters that still
    cannot be represented in ASCII are dropped.
    """
    translated = text.translate(get_table(lang))
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", translated)
    stripped = "".join(c for c in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(c))
    return stripped.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")

```python
"""Word-boundary-aware slug length limiting.

Slugs are often stored in columns or used in URLs and file names that have a
fixed maximum length. Cutting a slug at an arbitrary character produces
fragments such as ``introducing-the-new-pipel``. The helpers in this module
shorten a slug so that it fits the limit while preferring to end on a
complete word.

Two entry points are provided:

* ``truncate_slug`` works on an already built slug string.
* ``truncate_slug_parts`` works on a list of words and keeps as many whole
  words as fit.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Iterable, List

__all__ = ["TruncationError", "truncate_slug", "truncate_slug_parts"]

DEFAULT_SEPARATOR = "-"
DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH = 80


class TruncationError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a slug cannot be shortened under the requested rules."""


def _strip_trailing(value: str, separator: str) -> str:
    """Remove any separators left at the end of ``value`` after a cut."""
    while separator and value.endswith(separator):
        value = value.removesuffix(separator)
    return value


def truncate_slug(
    slug: str,
    max_length: int = DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH,
    separator: str = DEFAULT_SEPARATOR,
    *,
    word_boundary: bool = True,
    allow_hard_cut: bool = True,
) -> str:
    """Return ``slug`` limited to at most ``max_length`` characters.

    Parameters
    ----------
    slug:
        The slug to shorten. It is returned unchanged when it already fits.
    max_length:
        Maximum length of the result. Must be a positive integer.
    separator:
        The string that separates words inside the slug.
    word_boundary:
        When true, the slug is cut back to the last complete word that fits.
        When false, the slug is cut at exactly ``max_length`` characters.
    allow_hard_cut:
        Applies only when ``word_boundary`` is true and the first word alone
        is longer than the limit. If true, that word is cut at the limit.
        If false, ``TruncationError`` is raised instead.

    The result never ends with a separator.
    """
    if max_length < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_length must be a positive integer")
    if not separator:
        raise ValueError("separator must not be empty")

    if len(slug) <= max_length:
        return slug

    candidate = slug[:max_length]

    if word_boundary and not slug.startswith(separator, max_length):
        # The cut falls inside a word, so step back to the previous separator.
        last_separator = candidate.rfind(separator)
        if last_separator > 0:
            candidate = candidate[:last_separator]
        elif not allow_hard_cut:
            raise TruncationError(
                "first word of the slug is longer than max_length"
            )

    candidate = _strip_trailing(candidate, separator)
    if not candidate:
        raise TruncationError("nothing is left after removing separators")
    return candidate


def truncate_slug_parts(
    parts: Iterable[str],
    max_length: int = DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH,
    separator: str = DEFAULT_SEPARATOR,
    *,
    allow_hard_cut: bool = True,
) -> str:
    """Join ``parts`` with ``separator`` using only the words that fit.

    Words are added in order until the next word would make the joined
    string longer than ``max_length``. Empty parts are ignored. If not even
    the first word fits, behaviour follows ``allow_hard_cut`` in the same way
    as ``truncate_slug``.
    """
    if max_length < 1:
        raise ValueError("max_length must be a positive integer")

    kept: List[str] = []
    first_word = None

    for part in parts:
        if not part:
            continue
        if first_word is None:
            first_word = part
        if len(separator.join(kept + [part])) > max_length:
            break
        kept.append(part)

    if kept:
        return separator.join(kept)
    if first_word is None:
        return ""
    if not allow_hard_cut:
        raise TruncationError("first word is longer than max_length")

The file keeps argument parsing and dispatch in one place. Each subparser stores its handler with `set_defaults(handler=...)`, so `main` never needs a chain of conditionals on the command name. Adding a new command means registering one more subparser and writing one more handler in `cli.commands`.

Database location follows a fixed order of precedence: the `--db` flag, the `NOTES_DB` environment variable, and then the default path under the user's data directory. The parent directory is created when it does not exist, so the first run works without setup.

Error handling separates three cases. A failure to open the database returns exit code 2. A `CommandError` raised by a handler is a user-facing problem, such as an unknown note identifier, and returns 1. An interrupt returns the conventional shell code 130. The connection is always closed in the `finally` block, and the `with conn:` block commits changes when the handler succeeds and rolls them back when it raises.

Logging is sent to stderr so that exported data written to stdout can be piped into other tools without extra lines.

"""Argument parser construction for the ``notes`` command-line tool.

This module only describes the command-line interface. It does not open the
database or perform any work. Each subcommand stores its name in the
``command`` attribute of the parsed namespace, and the dispatcher in
``cli/main.py`` uses that value to select a handler.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Sequence

from notes import __version__

# The database location can be overridden with --db or NOTES_DB.
DEFAULT_DB = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "notes" / "notes.db"
EXPORT_FORMATS = ("json", "markdown", "csv")
SORT_ORDERS = ("created", "updated", "title")


def _add_global_flags(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    """Register flags that apply to every subcommand."""
    parser.add_argument(
        "--db",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(os.environ.get("NOTES_DB", DEFAULT_DB)),
        help="path to the SQLite database file (default: %(default)s)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="print extra diagnostic output to stderr",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--no-color",
        action="store_true",
        help="disable ANSI colors in output",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--version",
        action="version",
        version=f"%(prog)s {__version__}",
    )


def _add_add_command(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """``notes add``: create a new note from arguments or standard input."""
    p = sub.add_parser("add", help="create a new note")
    p.add_argument("title", help="short title for the note")
    p.add_argument(
        "-b", "--body",
        help="note text; if omitted, the body is read from standard input",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-t", "--tag",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="tags",
        metavar="TAG",
        help="attach a tag; may be given more than once",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-e", "--edit",
        action="store_true",
        help="open $EDITOR to write the body",
    )


def _add_tag_command(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """``notes tag``: add or remove tags on an existing note."""
    p = sub.add_parser("tag", help="add or remove tags on a note")
    p.add_argument("note_id", type=int, help="numeric id of the note")
    p.add_argument("tags", nargs="+", metavar="TAG", help="tags to apply")
    p.add_argument(
        "-r", "--remove",
        action="store_true",
        help="remove the given tags instead of adding them",
    )


def _add_search_command(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """``notes search``: full-text search with optional tag filtering."""
    p = sub.add_parser("search", help="search notes by text and tags")
    p.add_argument("query", nargs="?", default="", help="text to search for")
    p.add_argument(
        "-t", "--tag",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="tags",
        metavar="TAG",
        help="require this tag; may be given more than once",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--sort",
        choices=SORT_ORDERS,
        default="updated",
        help="ordering of results (default: %(default)s)",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-n", "--limit",
        type=int,
        default=20,
        help="maximum number of results (default: %(default)s)",
    )


def _add_export_command(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """``notes export``: write notes to a file or standard output."""
    p = sub.add_parser("export", help="export notes to a file")
    p.add_argument(
        "-f", "--format",

"""Command-line entry point for the personal notes tool.

This module builds the argument parser, registers one subparser per
command (add, tag, search, export), opens the SQLite database, and
dispatches to the matching handler. Handlers live in ``cli.commands``
and receive an open connection plus the parsed arguments. Each handler
returns an integer exit code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import os
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Sequence

from cli import commands
from notes.db import open_database

LOG = logging.getLogger("notes.cli")

# Environment variable that overrides the default database location.
DB_ENV_VAR = "NOTES_DB"
DEFAULT_DB_PATH = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "notes" / "notes.db"

Handler = Callable[[sqlite3.Connection, argparse.Namespace], int]


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Create the top-level parser and attach all subcommands."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="notes",
        description="Manage a personal notes database stored in SQLite.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--db",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="Path to the database file (default: $NOTES_DB or the user data directory).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable debug logging.",
    )

    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND")
    sub.required = True

    # add: create a new note, optionally with tags.
    p_add = sub.add_parser("add", help="Add a new note.")
    p_add.add_argument("text", nargs="?", help="Note body; read from stdin if omitted.")
    p_add.add_argument("-t", "--title", default=None, help="Optional note title.")
    p_add.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[], dest="tags",
                       help="Tag to attach; may be repeated.")
    p_add.set_defaults(handler=commands.cmd_add)

    # tag: attach or remove tags on an existing note.
    p_tag = sub.add_parser("tag", help="Add or remove tags on a note.")
    p_tag.add_argument("note_id", type=int, help="Identifier of the note.")
    p_tag.add_argument("tags", nargs="+", help="Tags to apply.")
    p_tag.add_argument("-r", "--remove", action="store_true",
                       help="Remove the tags instead of adding them.")
    p_tag.set_defaults(handler=commands.cmd_tag)

    # search: full-text query with optional tag filter.
    p_search = sub.add_parser("search", help="Search notes.")
    p_search.add_argument("query", help="Text to search for.")
    p_search.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[], dest="tags",
                          help="Restrict results to notes carrying this tag.")
    p_search.add_argument("-n", "--limit", type=int, default=20,
                          help="Maximum number of results to show.")
    p_search.set_defaults(handler=commands.cmd_search)

    # export: write notes to a file or standard output.
    p_export = sub.add_parser("export", help="Export notes.")
    p_export.add_argument("--format", choices=("json", "markdown", "csv"),
                          default="json", help="Output format.")
    p_export.add_argument("-o", "--output", type=Path, default=None,
                          help="Destination file; standard output if omitted.")
    p_export.set_defaults(handler=commands.cmd_export)

    return parser


def resolve_db_path(cli_value: Path | None) -> Path:
    """Pick the database path: command-line flag, then environment, then default."""
    if cli_value is not None:
        return cli_value
    env_value = os.environ.get(DB_ENV_VAR)
    if env_value:
        return Path(env_value).expanduser()
    return DEFAULT_DB_PATH


def configure_logging(verbose: bool) -> None:
    """Set up logging to stderr so stdout stays clean for exported data."""
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.WARNING,
        format="%(levelname)s: %(message)s",
        stream=sys.stderr,
    )


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Parse arguments, open the database, and run the chosen handler."""
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    configure_logging(args.verbose)

    db_path = resolve_db_path(args.db)
    db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    LOG.debug("Using database at %s", db_path)

    handler: Handler = args.handler
    try:
        conn = open_database(db_path)
    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
        print(f"error: cannot open database {db_path}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    try:
        with conn:  # commit on success, roll back on exception
            return handler(conn, args)
    except commands.CommandError as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 130
    finally:
        conn.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

The file keeps argument parsing and dispatch in one place. Each subparser stores its handler with `set_defaults(handler=...)`, so `main` never needs a chain of conditionals on the command name. Adding a new command means registering one more subparser and writing one more handler in `cli.commands`.

Database location follows a fixed order of precedence: the `--db` flag, the `NOTES_DB` environment variable, and then the default path under the user's data directory. The parent directory is created when it does not exist, so the first run works without setup.

Error handling separates three cases. A failure to open the database returns exit code 2. A `CommandError` raised by a handler is a user-facing problem, such as an unknown note identifier, and returns 1. An interrupt returns the conventional shell code 130. The connection is always closed in the `finally` block, and the `with conn:` block commits changes when the handler succeeds and rolls them back when it raises.

Logging is sent to stderr so that exported data written to stdout can be piped into other tools without extra lines.

```python
"""Handler for the ``add`` command.

A note body can come from three places, checked in this order:

1. Positional words on the command line (``notes add buy milk``).
2. Standard input, when it is piped or redirected.
3. The user's editor, when neither of the above supplies any text.

Tags given with ``--tag`` are normalized and attached to the new note in the
same transaction that creates it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from notes.db import open_database
from notes.errors import EmptyNoteError, NoteError
from notes.repository import NoteRepository
from notes.tags import normalize_tag

# Lines beginning with this marker are instructions for the user and are
# removed from editor content before the note is saved.
EDITOR_COMMENT_PREFIX = "#"

EDITOR_TEMPLATE = (
    "\n"
    "# Write your note above this line.\n"
    "# Lines starting with '#' are ignored.\n"
    "# Saving an empty file cancels the note.\n"
)


def register(subparsers: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """Attach the ``add`` sub-command and its options to the main parser."""
    parser = subparsers.add_parser("add", help="create a new note")
    parser.add_argument("text", nargs="*", help="note text; omit to use stdin or editor")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--title", help="explicit title (default: first line of body)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-g", "--tag", action="append", default=[], dest="tags",
        help="tag to attach; may be repeated",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e", "--edit", action="store_true",
        help="open the editor even if text was supplied, using it as initial content",
    )
    parser.set_defaults(handler=run)


def _read_stdin() -> str:
    """Return piped input, or an empty string when stdin is an interactive terminal."""
    if sys.stdin.isatty():
        return ""
    return sys.stdin.read()


def _editor_command() -> list[str]:
    """Pick the editor from VISUAL, then EDITOR, falling back to ``vi``."""
    configured = os.environ.get("VISUAL") or os.environ.get("EDITOR") or "vi"
    return shlex.split(configured)


def _strip_comments(raw: str) -> str:
    """Drop template comment lines and trim surrounding whitespace."""
    kept = [
        line for line in raw.splitlines()
        if not line.startswith(EDITOR_COMMENT_PREFIX)
    ]
    return "\n".join(kept).strip()


def _read_editor(initial: str = "") -> str:
    """Open the editor on a temporary file and return the saved content."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="notes-") as workdir:
        path = Path(workdir) / "NEW_NOTE.md"
        path.write_text(initial + EDITOR_TEMPLATE, encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            result = subprocess.run([*_editor_command(), str(path)], check=False)
        except FileNotFoundError as exc:
            raise NoteError(f"editor not found: {exc.filename}") from exc
        if result.returncode != 0:
            raise NoteError("editor exited with an error; note not saved")
        return _strip_comments(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _resolve_body(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    """Determine the note body according to the documented source order."""
    from_args = " ".join(args.text).strip()
    if args.edit:
        return _read_editor(from_args)
    if from_args:
        return from_args
    from_stdin = _read_stdin().strip()
    if from_stdin:
        return from_stdin
    return _read_editor()


def _split_title(body: str, explicit_title: str | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return ``(title, body)``, deriving the title from the first line if needed."""
    if explicit_title:
        return explicit_title.strip(), body
    first_line, _, remainder = body.partition("\n")
    title = first_line.lstrip("# ").strip()
    return title, (remainder.strip() or body)


def run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Execute the command and return a process exit status."""
    try:
        body = _resolve_body(args)
        if not body:
            raise EmptyNoteError("nothing to save; note was empty")

        title, body = _split_title(body, args.title)
        tags = sorted({normalize_tag(tag) for tag in args.tags})

        with open_database() as connection:
            repo = NoteRepository(connection)
            with connection:  # one transaction for the note and its tags
                note_id = repo.create(title=title, body=body)
                for tag in tags:
                    repo.attach_tag(note_id, tag)
    except NoteError as exc:
        print(f"notes: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    print(f"Created note {note_id}: {title}")
    return 0

        "--stdin",
        action="store_true",
        help="Read the new body from standard input",
    )
    parser.set_defaults(handler=run)


def run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Entry point called by the CLI dispatcher. Returns an exit code."""
    if args.body is not None and args.stdin:
        raise UsageError("--body and --stdin cannot be used together")

    conn = get_connection()
    try:
        note = _load_note(conn, args.note_id)

        new_title = args.title if args.title is not None else note.title
        new_body = note.body

        if args.body is not None:
            new_body = args.body
        elif args.stdin:
            new_body = sys.stdin.read()
        elif args.title is None:
            # No explicit change requested, so fall back to the editor.
            new_body = _edit_in_editor(note.body)

        new_title = new_title.strip()
        if not new_title:
            raise UsageError("A note title must not be empty")

        if new_title == note.title and new_body == note.body:
            print(f"Note {note.id} unchanged.")
            return 0

        _save_note(conn, note.id, new_title, new_body)
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()

    print(f"Note {note.id} updated.")
    return 0


def _load_note(conn, note_id: int) -> Note:
    """Fetch a note by primary key or raise NoteNotFoundError."""
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT id, title, body, created_at, updated_at "
        "FROM notes WHERE id = ?",
        (note_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise NoteNotFoundError(note_id)
    return Note(*row)


def _save_note(conn, note_id: int, title: str, body: str) -> None:
    """Write the new values and refresh the modification timestamp."""
    timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    conn.execute(
        "UPDATE notes SET title = ?, body = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
        (title, body, timestamp, note_id),
    )


def _edit_in_editor(initial_text: str) -> str:
    """Open the user's editor on a temporary file and return its content.

    The editor command is taken from $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, and finally
    defaults to ``vi``. The command string is split with shlex so that
    values such as ``code --wait`` work as expected.
    """
    editor = os.environ.get("VISUAL") or os.environ.get("EDITOR") or "vi"
    command = shlex.split(editor)

    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
        mode="w+", suffix=".md", delete=False, encoding="utf-8"
    ) as handle:
        handle.write(initial_text)
        path = handle.name

    try:
        result = subprocess.run([*command, path])
        if result.returncode != 0:
            raise UsageError(
                f"Editor exited with status {result.returncode}; "
                "note not modified"
            )
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            return handle.read()
    finally:
        # Always remove the temporary file, even if the editor failed.
        try:
            os.unlink(path)
        except OSError:
            pass
```

cli/commands/delete.py — Handler for soft- and hard-deleting notes with confirmation

"""Handler for the ``delete`` sub-command.

By default a note is soft-deleted: its ``deleted_at`` column is set and the
note is hidden from listing and search, but the row stays in the database
and can be restored. Passing ``--hard`` removes the note and its tag links
permanently. Both modes ask for confirmation unless ``--yes`` is given.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sqlite3
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Sequence

from cli.output import echo, error, warn
from notes.db import connect

EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_ABORTED = 1
EXIT_NOT_FOUND = 2


def register(subparsers: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """Attach the ``delete`` sub-command to the top-level parser."""
    parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "delete",
        help="delete one or more notes (soft delete by default)",
    )
    parser.add_argument("ids", nargs="+", type=int, help="IDs of notes to delete")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--hard",
        action="store_true",
        help="permanently remove the notes instead of hiding them",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-y", "--yes",
        action="store_true",
        help="skip the confirmation prompt",
    )
    parser.set_defaults(handler=run)


def _placeholders(items: Sequence[object]) -> str:
    """Return a comma-separated list of SQL placeholders, one per item."""
    return ",".join("?" for _ in items)


def _fetch_notes(conn: sqlite3.Connection, ids: Sequence[int]) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
    """Load the notes that exist and are not already soft-deleted."""
    query = (
        "SELECT id, title FROM notes "
        f"WHERE id IN ({_placeholders(ids)}) AND deleted_at IS NULL "
        "ORDER BY id"
    )
    return conn.execute(query, list(ids)).fetchall()


def _confirm(prompt: str, assume_yes: bool) -> bool:
    """Ask the user a yes/no question; the default answer is no.

    When stdin is not a terminal and ``--yes`` was not supplied, the
    deletion is refused so that scripts never destroy data by accident.
    """
    if assume_yes:
        return True
    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
        error("Refusing to delete without confirmation; use --yes in scripts.")
        return False
    answer = input(f"{prompt} [y/N]: ").strip().lower()
    return answer in ("y", "yes")


def _soft_delete(conn: sqlite3.Connection, ids: Sequence[int]) -> int:
    """Mark notes as deleted and return the number of rows changed."""
    stamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    cursor = conn.execute(
        f"UPDATE notes SET deleted_at = ? WHERE id IN ({_placeholders(ids)})",
        [stamp, *ids],
    )
    return cursor.rowcount


def _hard_delete(conn: sqlite3.Connection, ids: Sequence[int]) -> int:
    """Remove notes and their tag links from the database.

    Tag links are removed explicitly so the result does not depend on
    whether foreign-key cascades are enabled for this connection.
    """
    marks = _placeholders(ids)
    conn.execute(f"DELETE FROM note_tags WHERE note_id IN ({marks})", list(ids))
    cursor = conn.execute(f"DELETE FROM notes WHERE id IN ({marks})", list(ids))
    return cursor.rowcount


def run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Execute the ``delete`` command and return a process exit code."""
    requested = list(dict.fromkeys(args.ids))  # drop duplicates, keep order

    with connect() as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        found = _fetch_notes(conn, requested)
        found_ids = [row["id"] for row in found]

        missing = [note_id for note_id in requested if note_id not in found_ids]
        for note_id in missing:
            warn(f"No active note with id {note_id}; skipping.")

        if not found:
            error("Nothing to delete.")
            return EXIT_NOT_FOUND

        for row in found:
            echo(f"  #{row['id']}  {row['title']}")

        action = "Permanently delete" if args.hard else "Delete"
        noun = "note" if len(found) == 1 else "notes"
        if not _confirm(f"{action} {len(found)} {noun}?", args.yes):
            echo("Aborted. No notes were changed.")
            return EXIT_ABORTED

        # The connection context manager commits on success and rolls back
        # if an exception escapes, so both statements succeed or neither does.
        if args.hard:
            changed = _hard_delete(conn, found_ids)
            echo(f"Permanently deleted {changed} {noun}.")
        else:
            changed = _soft_delete(conn, found_ids)
            echo(f"Deleted {changed} {noun}. Use 'restore' to undo.")

    return EXIT_NOT_FOUND if missing else EXIT_OK

cli/commands/show.py — Handler for displaying a single note with metadata

"""Implementation of the ``notes show`` command.

Looks up one note by its integer id, gathers its tags and timestamps, and
prints it either as human-readable text or as JSON. The command is read-only
and never modifies the database.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sqlite3
import sys
import textwrap
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Optional

from cli.errors import NoteNotFoundError

EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_NOT_FOUND = 1

DATE_DISPLAY_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"


def register(subparsers: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """Attach the ``show`` subcommand to the top-level parser."""
    parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "show",
        help="display a single note with its metadata",
        description="Display one note, including tags and timestamps.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("note_id", type=int, help="id of the note to display")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--format",
        choices=("text", "json"),
        default="text",
        help="output format (default: text)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--no-meta",
        action="store_true",
        help="print only the title and body, without metadata",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--width",
        type=int,
        default=None,
        help="wrap the body at this column; by default the body is not wrapped",
    )
    parser.set_defaults(handler=handle_show)


def fetch_note(conn: sqlite3.Connection, note_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row:
    """Return the note row for ``note_id`` or raise NoteNotFoundError."""
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT id, title, body, created_at, updated_at "
        "FROM notes WHERE id = ?",
        (note_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise NoteNotFoundError(note_id)
    return row


def fetch_tags(conn: sqlite3.Connection, note_id: int) -> list[str]:
    """Return the tag names attached to a note, sorted alphabetically."""
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT t.name FROM tags AS t "
        "JOIN note_tags AS nt ON nt.tag_id = t.id "
        "WHERE nt.note_id = ? ORDER BY t.name",
        (note_id,),
    ).fetchall()
    return [r["name"] for r in rows]


def format_timestamp(value: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """Convert a stored ISO-8601 timestamp into a short display string.

    Values that cannot be parsed are returned unchanged so that a damaged
    row never prevents the note from being shown.
    """
    if not value:
        return "unknown"
    try:
        return datetime.fromisoformat(value).strftime(DATE_DISPLAY_FORMAT)
    except ValueError:
        return value


def wrap_body(body: str, width: Optional[int]) -> str:
    """Wrap each paragraph of ``body`` to ``width`` columns if requested."""
    if not width:
        return body
    paragraphs = body.split("\n\n")
    wrapped = [textwrap.fill(p, width=width) for p in paragraphs]
    return "\n\n".join(wrapped)


def render_text(note: sqlite3.Row, tags: list[str], args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    """Build the plain-text representation of a note."""
    lines = [note["title"]]
    if not args.no_meta:
        lines.append("-" * len(note["title"]))
        lines.append(f"id:       {note['id']}")
        lines.append(f"tags:     {', '.join(tags) if tags else '(none)'}")
        lines.append(f"created:  {format_timestamp(note['created_at'])}")
        lines.append(f"updated:  {format_timestamp(note['updated_at'])}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(wrap_body(note["body"] or "", args.width))
    return "\n".join(lines)


def render_json(note: sqlite3.Row, tags: list[str], args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    """Build the JSON representation of a note."""
    payload = {"id": note["id"], "title": note["title"], "body": note["body"]}
    if not args.no_meta:
        payload["tags"] = tags
        payload["created_at"] = note["created_at"]
        payload["updated_at"] = note["updated_at"]
    return json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)


def handle_show(args: argparse.Namespace, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int:
    """Entry point invoked by the dispatcher; returns a process exit code."""
    try:
        note = fetch_note(conn, args.note_id)
    except NoteNotFoundError:
        print(f"error: no note with id {args.note_id}", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_NOT_FOUND

    tags = fetch_tags(conn, note["id"])
    renderer = render_json if args.format == "json" else render_text
    print(renderer(note, tags, args))
    return EXIT_OK

cli/commands/list.py — Handler for listing notes with pagination and sorting

"""Handler for the ``list`` subcommand.

Prints a page of notes from the SQLite database, optionally filtered by
tag and sorted by creation time, modification time, or title. Output can
be rendered as a plain-text table or as JSON for use in scripts.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import sqlite3
import sys

from notes.db import connect
from notes.formatting import format_timestamp, truncate

DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 20
MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100

# Maps the user-facing sort key to a trusted SQL expression. Only values
# from this mapping are ever interpolated into the query text.
SORT_COLUMNS = {
    "created": "n.created_at",
    "updated": "n.updated_at",
    "title": "n.title COLLATE NOCASE",
}

# Time-based keys default to newest first; titles default to alphabetical.
DEFAULT_DIRECTION = {"created": "desc", "updated": "desc", "title": "asc"}


def register(subparsers: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """Attach the ``list`` subcommand and its options to the parser."""
    parser = subparsers.add_parser("list", help="List stored notes")
    parser.add_argument("--page", type=int, default=1,
                        help="page number, starting at 1")
    parser.add_argument("--page-size", type=int, default=DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE,
                        help="notes per page (maximum %d)" % MAX_PAGE_SIZE)
    parser.add_argument("--sort", choices=sorted(SORT_COLUMNS),
                        default="created", help="field to sort by")
    parser.add_argument("--order", choices=("asc", "desc"),
                        help="sort direction (default depends on --sort)")
    parser.add_argument("--tag", help="only show notes carrying this tag")
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", dest="as_json",
                        help="emit JSON instead of a table")
    parser.set_defaults(handler=run)


def _validate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    """Reject out-of-range paging values before touching the database."""
    if args.page < 1:
        raise SystemExit("error: --page must be at least 1")
    if not 1 <= args.page_size <= MAX_PAGE_SIZE:
        raise SystemExit(
            "error: --page-size must be between 1 and %d" % MAX_PAGE_SIZE
        )


def _build_filter(tag: str | None) -> tuple[str, list]:
    """Return a WHERE clause and its bound parameters for the tag filter."""
    if tag is None:
        return "", []
    clause = (
        "WHERE n.id IN ("
        "SELECT nt2.note_id FROM note_tags nt2 "
        "JOIN tags t2 ON t2.id = nt2.tag_id WHERE t2.name = ?)"
    )
    return clause, [tag.strip().lower()]


def fetch_page(conn: sqlite3.Connection, args: argparse.Namespace):
    """Fetch one page of notes and the total number of matching notes."""
    where, params = _build_filter(args.tag)
    direction = args.order or DEFAULT_DIRECTION[args.sort]
    order_by = "%s %s, n.id ASC" % (SORT_COLUMNS[args.sort], direction.upper())
    offset = (args.page - 1) * args.page_size

    total = conn.execute(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notes n %s" % where, params
    ).fetchone()[0]

    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT n.id, n.title, n.created_at, n.updated_at, "
        "COALESCE(GROUP_CONCAT(t.name, ','), '') AS tags "
        "FROM notes n "
        "LEFT JOIN note_tags nt ON nt.note_id = n.id "
        "LEFT JOIN tags t ON t.id = nt.tag_id "
        "%s GROUP BY n.id ORDER BY %s LIMIT ? OFFSET ?" % (where, order_by),
        params + [args.page_size, offset],
    ).fetchall()
    return rows, total


def _print_table(rows, page: int, pages: int, total: int) -> None:
    """Render rows as an aligned text table followed by a paging footer."""
    if not rows:
        print("No notes found.")
        return
    print("%-6s %-40s %-16s %s" % ("ID", "TITLE", "UPDATED", "TAGS"))
    for row in rows:
        print("%-6d %-40s %-16s %s" % (
            row["id"],
            truncate(row["title"], 40),
            format_timestamp(row["updated_at"]),
            row["tags"].replace(",", ", "),
        ))
    print("\nPage %d of %d (%d notes)" % (page, pages, total))


def _print_json(rows, page: int, pages: int, total: int) -> None:
    """Render the page as a JSON document on standard output."""
    payload = {
        "page": page,
        "pages": pages,
        "total": total,
        "notes": [
            {
                "id": row["id"],
                "title": row["title"],
                "created_at": row["created_at"],
                "updated_at": row["updated_at"],
                "tags": [t for t in row["tags"].split(",") if t],
            }
            for row in rows
        ],
    }
    json.dump(payload, sys.stdout, indent=2)
    sys.stdout.write("\n")


def run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Execute the ``list`` command and return a process exit code."""
    _validate(args)
    with connect() as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        rows, total = fetch_page(conn, args)

    pages = max(1, math.ceil(total / args.page_size))
    if args.page > pages:
        print("error: page %d is past the last page (%d)" % (args.page, pages),
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    printer = _print_json if args.as_json else _print_table
    printer(rows, args.page, pages, total)
    return 0

cli/commands/tag.py — Handler for adding and removing tags on notes

"""Handler for the ``tag`` command.

Usage:
    notes tag add NOTE_ID TAG [TAG ...]
    notes tag remove NOTE_ID TAG [TAG ...]

Tags are stored in the ``tags`` table and linked to notes through the
``note_tags`` join table. Tag names are normalized before they are written,
so "Work", " work " and "WORK" all refer to the same tag.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import sqlite3
import sys

from notes.db import connect
from notes.errors import NoteNotFoundError, InvalidTagError

MAX_TAG_LENGTH = 40
_TAG_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_\-]*$")


def register(subparsers: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """Attach the ``tag`` command and its sub-actions to the main parser."""
    parser = subparsers.add_parser("tag", help="add or remove tags on a note")
    actions = parser.add_subparsers(dest="action", required=True)

    add_parser = actions.add_parser("add", help="attach tags to a note")
    add_parser.add_argument("note_id", type=int)
    add_parser.add_argument("tags", nargs="+")

    remove_parser = actions.add_parser("remove", help="detach tags from a note")
    remove_parser.add_argument("note_id", type=int)
    remove_parser.add_argument("tags", nargs="+")

    parser.set_defaults(handler=run)


def normalize_tag(raw: str) -> str:
    """Return the canonical form of a tag name or raise InvalidTagError.

    Surrounding whitespace is removed, the text is lowercased, and inner
    whitespace runs become a single hyphen.
    """
    name = re.sub(r"\s+", "-", raw.strip().lower())
    if not name:
        raise InvalidTagError("tag name must not be empty")
    if len(name) > MAX_TAG_LENGTH:
        raise InvalidTagError(
            f"tag '{name}' exceeds the limit of {MAX_TAG_LENGTH} characters"
        )
    if not _TAG_PATTERN.match(name):
        raise InvalidTagError(
            f"tag '{name}' may only contain letters, digits, '-' and '_'"
        )
    return name


def _normalize_all(raw_tags: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Normalize a list of tags, dropping duplicates but keeping order."""
    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
    for raw in raw_tags:
        seen.setdefault(normalize_tag(raw), None)
    return list(seen)


def _require_note(conn: sqlite3.Connection, note_id: int) -> None:
    row = conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM notes WHERE id = ?", (note_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise NoteNotFoundError(note_id)


def _get_or_create_tag_id(conn: sqlite3.Connection, name: str) -> int:
    """Look up a tag by name, inserting it first if it does not exist."""
    conn.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO tags (name) VALUES (?)", (name,))
    row = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM tags WHERE name = ?", (name,)).fetchone()
    return row[0]


def add_tags(conn: sqlite3.Connection, note_id: int, tags: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Attach tags to a note and return the ones that were newly linked."""
    added = []
    for name in tags:
        tag_id = _get_or_create_tag_id(conn, name)
        cursor = conn.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO note_tags (note_id, tag_id) VALUES (?, ?)",
            (note_id, tag_id),
        )
        if cursor.rowcount:
            added.append(name)
    return added


def remove_tags(conn: sqlite3.Connection, note_id: int, tags: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Detach tags from a note and return the ones that were actually linked."""
    removed = []
    for name in tags:
        cursor = conn.execute(
            "DELETE FROM note_tags WHERE note_id = ? AND tag_id = "
            "(SELECT id FROM tags WHERE name = ?)",
            (note_id, name),
        )
        if cursor.rowcount:
            removed.append(name)
    # Remove tags that no note uses any longer so the tag list stays clean.
    conn.execute(
        "DELETE FROM tags WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT tag_id FROM note_tags)"
    )
    return removed


def run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Entry point called by the dispatcher. Returns a process exit code."""
    try:
        tags = _normalize_all(args.tags)
    except InvalidTagError as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    conn = connect()
    try:
        with conn:  # one transaction: commit on success, roll back on error
            _require_note(conn, args.note_id)
            if args.action == "add":
                changed = add_tags(conn, args.note_id, tags)
                verb = "Added"
            else:
                changed = remove_tags(conn, args.note_id, tags)
                verb = "Removed"
    except NoteNotFoundError:
        print(f"error: no note with id {args.note_id}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    finally:
        conn.close()

    if changed:
        print(f"{verb} on note {args.note_id}: {', '.join(changed)}")
    else:
        print(f"No changes made to note {args.note_id}.")
    return 0

cli/commands/search.py — Handler for full-text and filtered note search

"""Handler for the ``search`` subcommand.

Supports full-text queries against the FTS5 index (``notes_fts``), combined
with optional tag and date filters. Results can be printed as a table,
JSON, or a bare list of note ids for use in shell pipelines.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sqlite3
import sys
from datetime import date

from cli.db import connect

DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
EXCERPT_CHARS = 80
OUTPUT_FORMATS = ("table", "json", "ids")


def register(subparsers: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """Attach the ``search`` subcommand and its options to the main parser."""
    p = subparsers.add_parser("search", help="search notes by text, tag or date")
    p.add_argument("query", nargs="*", help="words to look for in title and body")
    p.add_argument("-t", "--tag", action="append", default=[],
                   help="require this tag; repeat the option to require several")
    p.add_argument("--since", type=date.fromisoformat, metavar="YYYY-MM-DD",
                   help="only notes updated on or after this date")
    p.add_argument("--until", type=date.fromisoformat, metavar="YYYY-MM-DD",
                   help="only notes updated on or before this date")
    p.add_argument("--raw", action="store_true",
                   help="pass the query to FTS5 unchanged (enables AND/OR/NEAR)")
    p.add_argument("-n", "--limit", type=int, default=DEFAULT_LIMIT)
    p.add_argument("-f", "--format", choices=OUTPUT_FORMATS, default="table")
    p.set_defaults(handler=run)


def _quote_terms(words: list[str]) -> str:
    """Turn plain words into quoted FTS5 phrases so punctuation is harmless."""
    return " ".join('"' + w.replace('"', '""') + '"' for w in words)


def build_query(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, list]:
    """Return the SQL text and bound parameters for the given arguments."""
    params: list = []
    where: list[str] = []

    if args.query:
        match = " ".join(args.query) if args.raw else _quote_terms(args.query)
        select = ("SELECT n.id, n.title, n.updated_at, "
                  "snippet(notes_fts, 1, '[', ']', '...', 12) AS excerpt "
                  "FROM notes_fts JOIN notes n ON n.id = notes_fts.rowid ")
        where.append("notes_fts MATCH ?")
        params.append(match)
        order = "ORDER BY bm25(notes_fts)"
    else:
        select = ("SELECT n.id, n.title, n.updated_at, "
                  "substr(n.body, 1, ?) AS excerpt FROM notes n ")
        params.append(EXCERPT_CHARS)
        order = "ORDER BY n.updated_at DESC"

    for tag in args.tag:
        where.append(
            "EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM note_tags nt JOIN tags t ON t.id = nt.tag_id "
            "WHERE nt.note_id = n.id AND t.name = ?)"
        )
        params.append(tag.lower())

    if args.since:
        where.append("date(n.updated_at) >= ?")
        params.append(args.since.isoformat())
    if args.until:
        where.append("date(n.updated_at) <= ?")
        params.append(args.until.isoformat())

    sql = select
    if where:
        sql += "WHERE " + " AND ".join(where) + " "
    sql += order + " LIMIT ?"
    params.append(args.limit)
    return sql, params


def _print_table(rows: list[sqlite3.Row]) -> None:
    """Print results as aligned columns: id, updated date, title, excerpt."""
    id_width = max(len(str(r["id"])) for r in rows)
    for r in rows:
        excerpt = " ".join((r["excerpt"] or "").split())
        print(f"{r['id']:>{id_width}}  {r['updated_at'][:10]}  "
              f"{r['title']}  {excerpt}")


def run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Execute the search and print results. Exit status 1 means no matches."""
    if args.limit < 1:
        print("error: --limit must be a positive integer", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if args.since and args.until and args.since > args.until:
        print("error: --since is later than --until", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    sql, params = build_query(args)
    try:
        with connect() as conn:
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            rows = conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
    except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
        # Raw FTS5 syntax errors surface here as OperationalError.
        print(f"error: search failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    if not rows:
        return 1

    if args.format == "json":
        json.dump([dict(r) for r in rows], sys.stdout, indent=2)
        print()
    elif args.format == "ids":
        for r in rows:
            print(r["id"])
    else:
        _print_table(rows)
    return 0

"""Export command for the notes CLI.

Writes notes from the SQLite database to a file or to standard output in
one of three formats: JSON, Markdown, or CSV. Notes can be filtered by tag
before export.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Iterator, TextIO

from notes.db import connect, fetch_notes
from notes.models import Note

SUPPORTED_FORMATS = ("json", "markdown", "csv")
CSV_FIELDS = ("id", "title", "body", "tags", "created_at", "updated_at")


def register(subparsers: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """Attach the ``export`` subcommand to the top-level parser."""
    parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "export", help="Export notes to JSON, Markdown, or CSV"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-f", "--format",
        choices=SUPPORTED_FORMATS,
        default="json",
        help="Output format (default: json)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-o", "--output",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="Destination file. Writes to standard output if omitted.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-t", "--tag",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        help="Only export notes carrying this tag. May be repeated.",
    )
    parser.set_defaults(handler=handle)


def handle(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Run the export command and return a process exit code."""
    with connect(args.db_path) as conn:
        notes = fetch_notes(conn, tags=args.tag or None)

    if not notes:
        print("No notes matched; nothing to export.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    writer = WRITERS[args.format]
    try:
        with open_destination(args.output) as stream:
            writer(notes, stream)
    except OSError as exc:
        print(f"Could not write export: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    if args.output is not None:
        print(f"Exported {len(notes)} notes to {args.output}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


@contextmanager
def open_destination(path: Path | None) -> Iterator[TextIO]:
    """Yield an open text stream for ``path``, or stdout when it is None.

    Files are opened with UTF-8 encoding and ``newline=""`` so that the
    csv module controls line endings itself.
    """
    if path is None:
        yield sys.stdout
        return
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        yield stream


def note_to_dict(note: Note) -> dict:
    """Convert a Note into a plain dictionary with ISO 8601 timestamps."""
    return {
        "id": note.id,
        "title": note.title,
        "body": note.body,
        "tags": sorted(note.tags),
        "created_at": note.created_at.isoformat(),
        "updated_at": note.updated_at.isoformat(),
    }


def write_json(notes: Iterable[Note], stream: TextIO) -> None:
    """Write all notes as a single JSON array."""
    payload = [note_to_dict(n) for n in notes]
    json.dump(payload, stream, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    stream.write("\n")


def write_markdown(notes: Iterable[Note], stream: TextIO) -> None:
    """Write each note as a level-two heading followed by its body.

    Tags are listed on a separate line beneath the heading, and notes are
    separated by a horizontal rule.
    """
    for note in notes:
        stream.write(f"## {note.title}\n\n")
        if note.tags:
            tag_line = ", ".join(f"`{t}`" for t in sorted(note.tags))
            stream.write(f"Tags: {tag_line}\n\n")
        stream.write(f"*Created {note.created_at:%Y-%m-%d}*\n\n")
        stream.write(note.body.rstrip() + "\n\n---\n\n")


def write_csv(notes: Iterable[Note], stream: TextIO) -> None:
    """Write notes as CSV with a header row.

    Tags are joined with semicolons so they fit in a single column.
    """
    writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=CSV_FIELDS)
    writer.writeheader()
    for note in notes:
        row = note_to_dict(note)
        row["tags"] = ";".join(row["tags"])
        writer.writerow(row)


WRITERS = {
    "json": write_json,
    "markdown": write_markdown,
    "csv": write_csv,
}

```python
"""Import command: load notes from JSON, Markdown, or plain-text files.

Usage examples:
    notes import backup.json
    notes import ~/journal --format markdown --tag journal
    notes import todo.txt --dry-run

Markdown files may start with a simple front-matter block delimited by
lines containing only "---". Recognised keys are "title" and "tags"
(a comma-separated list).
"""

import argparse
import json
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from notes.db import connect, insert_note, attach_tag, note_exists
from notes.errors import ImportFormatError

SUPPORTED_FORMATS = ("json", "markdown", "text")
MARKDOWN_SUFFIXES = {".md", ".markdown"}


def register(subparsers):
    """Attach the 'import' sub-command to the main argument parser."""
    parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "import", help="import notes from external files"
    )
    parser.add_argument("path", type=Path, help="file or directory to import")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--format", choices=SUPPORTED_FORMATS, default=None,
        help="input format (guessed from the file suffix when omitted)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--tag", action="append", default=[],
        help="tag to add to every imported note (may be repeated)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--skip-duplicates", action="store_true",
        help="skip notes whose title and body already exist",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dry-run", action="store_true",
        help="parse the input and report results without writing",
    )
    parser.set_defaults(handler=run)


def guess_format(path):
    """Return the format name implied by a file's suffix."""
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix == ".json":
        return "json"
    if suffix in MARKDOWN_SUFFIXES:
        return "markdown"
    return "text"


def parse_json(path):
    """Yield note dicts from a JSON file holding a list of objects."""
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        raise ImportFormatError(f"{path}: expected a top-level list")
    for item in data:
        if not isinstance(item, dict) or "body" not in item:
            raise ImportFormatError(f"{path}: entry without a 'body' field")
        yield {
            "title": item.get("title") or path.stem,
            "body": item["body"],
            "tags": list(item.get("tags", [])),
        }


def parse_markdown(path):
    """Yield one note from a Markdown file, reading optional front matter."""
    lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    meta = {}
    if lines and lines[0].strip() == "---":
        for index, line in enumerate(lines[1:], start=1):
            if line.strip() == "---":
                lines = lines[index + 1:]
                break
            key, _, value = line.partition(":")
            meta[key.strip().lower()] = value.strip()
    tags = [t.strip() for t in meta.get("tags", "").split(",") if t.strip()]
    yield {
        "title": meta.get("title") or path.stem,
        "body": "\n".join(lines).strip(),
        "tags": tags,
    }


def parse_text(path):
    """Yield one note per file, using the file name as the title."""
    yield {
        "title": path.stem,
        "body": path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip(),
        "tags": [],
    }


PARSERS = {"json": parse_json, "markdown": parse_markdown, "text": parse_text}


def collect_files(path):
    """Return the files to import: the path itself or a directory's files."""
    if path.is_dir():
        return sorted(p for p in path.iterdir() if p.is_file())
    return [path]


def run(args):
    """Execute the import and return a process exit code."""
    if not args.path.exists():
        print(f"error: {args.path} does not exist", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    imported = skipped = failed = 0
    conn = connect()
    try:
        for file_path in collect_files(args.path):
            fmt = args.format or guess_format(file_path)
            try:
                notes = list(PARSERS[fmt](file_path))
            except (ImportFormatError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
                print(f"warning: {file_path}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
                failed += 1
                continue

            for note in notes:
                if args.skip_duplicates and note_exists(
                    conn, note["title"], note["body"]
                ):
                    skipped += 1
                    continue
                if not args.dry_run:
                    note_id = insert_note(conn, note["title"], note["body"])
                    for tag in note["tags"] + args.tag:
                        attach_tag(conn, note_id, tag)
                imported += 1
        if args.dry_run:
            conn.rollback()
        else:
            conn.commit()
    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
        conn.rollback()
        print(f"database error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    finally:
        conn.close()

    label = "would import" if args.dry_run else "imported"
    print(f"{label}: {imported}, skipped: {skipped}, failed files: {failed}")
    return 0 if failed == 0 else 1

# cli/main.py — Entry point that wires argument parsing to command handlers

```python
"""Command-line entry point for the personal notes tool.

This module builds the argument parser, registers one subparser per
command (add, tag, search, export), opens the SQLite database, and
dispatches to the matching handler. Handlers live in ``cli.commands``
and receive an open connection plus the parsed arguments. Each handler
returns an integer exit code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import os
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Sequence

from cli import commands
from notes.db import open_database

LOG = logging.getLogger("notes.cli")

# Environment variable that overrides the default database location.
DB_ENV_VAR = "NOTES_DB"
DEFAULT_DB_PATH = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "notes" / "notes.db"

Handler = Callable[[sqlite3.Connection, argparse.Namespace], int]


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Create the top-level parser and attach all subcommands."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="notes",
        description="Manage a personal notes database stored in SQLite.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--db",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="Path to the database file (default: $NOTES_DB or the user data directory).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable debug logging.",
    )

    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND")
    sub.required = True

    # add: create a new note, optionally with tags.
    p_add = sub.add_parser("add", help="Add a new note.")
    p_add.add_argument("text", nargs="?", help="Note body; read from stdin if omitted.")
    p_add.add_argument("-t", "--title", default=None, help="Optional note title.")
    p_add.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[], dest="tags",
                       help="Tag to attach; may be repeated.")
    p_add.set_defaults(handler=commands.cmd_add)

    # tag: attach or remove tags on an existing note.
    p_tag = sub.add_parser("tag", help="Add or remove tags on a note.")
    p_tag.add_argument("note_id", type=int, help="Identifier of the note.")
    p_tag.add_argument("tags", nargs="+", help="Tags to apply.")
    p_tag.add_argument("-r", "--remove", action="store_true",
                       help="Remove the tags instead of adding them.")
    p_tag.set_defaults(handler=commands.cmd_tag)

    # search: full-text query with optional tag filter.
    p_search = sub.add_parser("search", help="Search notes.")
    p_search.add_argument("query", help="Text to search for.")
    p_search.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[], dest="tags",
                          help="Restrict results to notes carrying this tag.")
    p_search.add_argument("-n", "--limit", type=int, default=20,
                          help="Maximum number of results to show.")
    p_search.set_defaults(handler=commands.cmd_search)

    # export: write notes to a file or standard output.
    p_export = sub.add_parser("export", help="Export notes.")
    p_export.add_argument("--format", choices=("json", "markdown", "csv"),
                          default="json", help="Output format.")
    p_export.add_argument("-o", "--output", type=Path, default=None,
                          help="Destination file; standard output if omitted.")
    p_export.set_defaults(handler=commands.cmd_export)

    return parser


def resolve_db_path(cli_value: Path | None) -> Path:
    """Pick the database path: command-line flag, then environment, then default."""
    if cli_value is not None:
        return cli_value
    env_value = os.environ.get(DB_ENV_VAR)
    if env_value:
        return Path(env_value).expanduser()
    return DEFAULT_DB_PATH


def configure_logging(verbose: bool) -> None:
    """Set up logging to stderr so stdout stays clean for exported data."""
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.WARNING,
        format="%(levelname)s: %(message)s",
        stream=sys.stderr,
    )


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Parse arguments, open the database, and run the chosen handler."""
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    configure_logging(args.verbose)

    db_path = resolve_db_path(args.db)
    db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    LOG.debug("Using database at %s", db_path)

    handler: Handler = args.handler
    try:
        conn = open_database(db_path)
    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
        print(f"error: cannot open database {db_path}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    try:
        with conn:  # commit on success, roll back on exception
            return handler(conn, args)
    except commands.CommandError as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 130
    finally:
        conn.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

The file keeps argument parsing and dispatch in one place. Each subparser stores its handler with `set_defaults(handler=...)`, so `main` never needs a chain of conditionals on the command name. Adding a new command means registering one more subparser and writing one more handler in `cli.commands`.

Database location follows a fixed order of precedence: the `--db` flag, the `NOTES_DB` environment variable, and then the default path under the user's data directory. The parent directory is created when it does not exist, so the first run works without setup.

Error handling separates three cases. A failure to open the database returns exit code 2. A `CommandError` raised by a handler is a user-facing problem, such as an unknown note identifier, and returns 1. An interrupt returns the conventional shell code 130. The connection is always closed in the `finally` block, and the `with conn:` block commits changes when the handler succeeds and rolls them back when it raises.

Logging is sent to stderr so that exported data written to stdout can be piped into other tools without extra lines.

"""Argument parser construction for the ``notes`` command-line tool.

This module only describes the command-line interface. It does not open the
database or perform any work. Each subcommand stores its name in the
``command`` attribute of the parsed namespace, and the dispatcher in
``cli/main.py`` uses that value to select a handler.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Sequence

from notes import __version__

# The database location can be overridden with --db or NOTES_DB.
DEFAULT_DB = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "notes" / "notes.db"
EXPORT_FORMATS = ("json", "markdown", "csv")
SORT_ORDERS = ("created", "updated", "title")


def _add_global_flags(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    """Register flags that apply to every subcommand."""
    parser.add_argument(
        "--db",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(os.environ.get("NOTES_DB", DEFAULT_DB)),
        help="path to the SQLite database file (default: %(default)s)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="print extra diagnostic output to stderr",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--no-color",
        action="store_true",
        help="disable ANSI colors in output",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--version",
        action="version",
        version=f"%(prog)s {__version__}",
    )


def _add_add_command(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """``notes add``: create a new note from arguments or standard input."""
    p = sub.add_parser("add", help="create a new note")
    p.add_argument("title", help="short title for the note")
    p.add_argument(
        "-b", "--body",
        help="note text; if omitted, the body is read from standard input",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-t", "--tag",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="tags",
        metavar="TAG",
        help="attach a tag; may be given more than once",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-e", "--edit",
        action="store_true",
        help="open $EDITOR to write the body",
    )


def _add_tag_command(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """``notes tag``: add or remove tags on an existing note."""
    p = sub.add_parser("tag", help="add or remove tags on a note")
    p.add_argument("note_id", type=int, help="numeric id of the note")
    p.add_argument("tags", nargs="+", metavar="TAG", help="tags to apply")
    p.add_argument(
        "-r", "--remove",
        action="store_true",
        help="remove the given tags instead of adding them",
    )


def _add_search_command(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """``notes search``: full-text search with optional tag filtering."""
    p = sub.add_parser("search", help="search notes by text and tags")
    p.add_argument("query", nargs="?", default="", help="text to search for")
    p.add_argument(
        "-t", "--tag",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="tags",
        metavar="TAG",
        help="require this tag; may be given more than once",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--sort",
        choices=SORT_ORDERS,
        default="updated",
        help="ordering of results (default: %(default)s)",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-n", "--limit",
        type=int,
        default=20,
        help="maximum number of results (default: %(default)s)",
    )


def _add_export_command(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """``notes export``: write notes to a file or standard output."""
    p = sub.add_parser("export", help="export notes to a file")
    p.add_argument(
        "-f", "--format",
        choices=EXPORT_FORMATS,
        default="json",
        help="output format (default: %(default)s)",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-o", "--output",
        type=Path,
        help="destination file; standard output is used if omitted",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-t", "--tag",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="tags",
        metavar="TAG",
        help="export only notes carrying this tag",
    )


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Return the fully configured top-level parser."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="notes",
        description="Manage a personal notes database stored in SQLite.",
    )
    _add_global_flags(parser)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND")
    sub.required = True
    _add_add_command(sub)
    _add_tag_command(sub)
    _add_search_command(sub)
    _add_export_command(sub)
    return parser


def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    """Parse ``argv`` (or ``sys.argv`` when None) into a namespace."""
    return build_parser().parse_args(argv)

```python
"""Command-line interface package for the personal notes manager.

This package contains the argument parsing, command dispatch, and output
formatting used by the ``notes`` executable. The storage layer lives in a
separate package and is not imported here, so that importing ``cli`` stays
inexpensive and does not open a database connection.

Typical usage from another module::

    from cli import main, __version__

    exit_code = main(["add", "Buy milk", "--tag", "errands"])

The names listed in ``__all__`` form the public API of this package. Anything
not listed there may change between releases without notice.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Version information
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The version string follows the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH convention. Packaging
# metadata reads this value, so it should be edited only here.
__version__ = "0.4.0"

# A tuple form is provided so that callers can compare versions without
# parsing the string.
VERSION_INFO = (0, 4, 0)

__author__ = "Notes CLI contributors"
__license__ = "MIT"

# Name of the executable as it appears in help text and error messages.
PROG_NAME = "notes"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exit codes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Exit codes are shared by every subcommand so that shell scripts can react
# to specific failures. They are defined here so that submodules and tests
# import them from a single location.
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_ERROR = 1
EXIT_USAGE = 2
EXIT_NOT_FOUND = 3
EXIT_DB_ERROR = 4

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lazy public API
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Maps each lazily exposed name to the submodule that defines it. Resolving
# names on first access keeps ``import cli`` fast, which matters for shell
# completion and for the ``--version`` flag.
_LAZY_EXPORTS = {
    "main": "cli.app",
    "build_parser": "cli.parser",
    "CommandError": "cli.errors",
    "format_note": "cli.output",
}

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover - imports used only by type checkers
    from cli.app import main
    from cli.errors import CommandError
    from cli.output import format_note
    from cli.parser import build_parser

__all__ = [
    "__version__",
    "VERSION_INFO",
    "PROG_NAME",
    "EXIT_OK",
    "EXIT_ERROR",
    "EXIT_USAGE",
    "EXIT_NOT_FOUND",
    "EXIT_DB_ERROR",
    "main",
    "build_parser",
    "CommandError",
    "format_note",
    "version_string",
]


def version_string() -> str:
    """Return the text printed by ``notes --version``."""
    return f"{PROG_NAME} {__version__}"


def __getattr__(name: str) -> Any:
    """Resolve public names from submodules on first access (PEP 562).

    The resolved object is stored in the module namespace so that later
    lookups bypass this function.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If ``name`` is not part of the public API.
    """
    module_path = _LAZY_EXPORTS.get(name)
    if module_path is None:
        raise AttributeError(f"module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}")
    module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
    value = getattr(module, name)
    globals()[name] = value
    return value


def __dir__() -> list[str]:
    """Include lazily exposed names in ``dir(cli)`` and tab completion."""
    return sorted(set(globals()) | set(__all__))
```

This file deliberately keeps the package marker small. Version data, exit codes, and the program name are plain module-level values, while the larger pieces of the interface are loaded only when requested. The `__getattr__` hook follows PEP 562, and `__dir__` keeps interactive discovery consistent with the declared public API. The `TYPE_CHECKING` block gives static analysis tools the real import locations without running those imports at runtime.

cli/commands/add.py — Handler for creating a new note from args, stdin, or editor

```python
"""Handler for the ``add`` command.

A note body can come from three places, checked in this order:

1. Positional words on the command line (``notes add buy milk``).
2. Standard input, when it is piped or redirected.
3. The user's editor, when neither of the above supplies any text.

Tags given with ``--tag`` are normalized and attached to the new note in the
same transaction that creates it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from notes.db import open_database
from notes.errors import EmptyNoteError, NoteError
from notes.repository import NoteRepository
from notes.tags import normalize_tag

# Lines beginning with this marker are instructions for the user and are
# removed from editor content before the note is saved.
EDITOR_COMMENT_PREFIX = "#"

EDITOR_TEMPLATE = (
    "\n"
    "# Write your note above this line.\n"
    "# Lines starting with '#' are ignored.\n"
    "# Saving an empty file cancels the note.\n"
)


def register(subparsers: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """Attach the ``add`` sub-command and its options to the main parser."""
    parser = subparsers.add_parser("add", help="create a new note")
    parser.add_argument("text", nargs="*", help="note text; omit to use stdin or editor")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--title", help="explicit title (default: first line of body)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-g", "--tag", action="append", default=[], dest="tags",
        help="tag to attach; may be repeated",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e", "--edit", action="store_true",
        help="open the editor even if text was supplied, using it as initial content",
    )
    parser.set_defaults(handler=run)


def _read_stdin() -> str:
    """Return piped input, or an empty string when stdin is an interactive terminal."""
    if sys.stdin.isatty():
        return ""
    return sys.stdin.read()


def _editor_command() -> list[str]:
    """Pick the editor from VISUAL, then EDITOR, falling back to ``vi``."""
    configured = os.environ.get("VISUAL") or os.environ.get("EDITOR") or "vi"
    return shlex.split(configured)


def _strip_comments(raw: str) -> str:
    """Drop template comment lines and trim surrounding whitespace."""
    kept = [
        line for line in raw.splitlines()
        if not line.startswith(EDITOR_COMMENT_PREFIX)
    ]
    return "\n".join(kept).strip()


def _read_editor(initial: str = "") -> str:
    """Open the editor on a temporary file and return the saved content."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="notes-") as workdir:
        path = Path(workdir) / "NEW_NOTE.md"
        path.write_text(initial + EDITOR_TEMPLATE, encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            result = subprocess.run([*_editor_command(), str(path)], check=False)
        except FileNotFoundError as exc:
            raise NoteError(f"editor not found: {exc.filename}") from exc
        if result.returncode != 0:
            raise NoteError("editor exited with an error; note not saved")
        return _strip_comments(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _resolve_body(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    """Determine the note body according to the documented source order."""
    from_args = " ".join(args.text).strip()
    if args.edit:
        return _read_editor(from_args)
    if from_args:
        return from_args
    from_stdin = _read_stdin().strip()
    if from_stdin:
        return from_stdin
    return _read_editor()


def _split_title(body: str, explicit_title: str | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return ``(title, body)``, deriving the title from the first line if needed."""
    if explicit_title:
        return explicit_title.strip(), body
    first_line, _, remainder = body.partition("\n")
    title = first_line.lstrip("# ").strip()
    return title, (remainder.strip() or body)


def run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Execute the command and return a process exit status."""
    try:
        body = _resolve_body(args)
        if not body:
            raise EmptyNoteError("nothing to save; note was empty")

        title, body = _split_title(body, args.title)
        tags = sorted({normalize_tag(tag) for tag in args.tags})

        with open_database() as connection:
